reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a recurring motif of sharp, narrow positive spikes (amplitude ~35–45 robust-standardized units) followed by rapid decay to near-zero baseline, with inter-spike intervals of roughly 10–12 points. Each spike is approximately 2–3 points wide at base and symmetric or slightly right-skewed; troughs are flat and stable near zero, occasionally dipping slightly negative. The underlying baseline is stable (median near 0), with no persistent trend across candidates—slope_per_point values range from -1.3 to +0.06, but visual inspection shows only transient local slopes, not global drift. Noise is low during quiescent phases (MAD 0.13–0.61), though roughness increases with window length due to inclusion of more spikes. Amplitude_90 (~39–41) reflects the consistent spike height; curvature is high during spikes (>14 in longer windows) but near-zero elsewhere. The pattern is periodic with estimated period ~10, matching the catalog’s window_cycles scaling: candidate 0 shows 1 cycle (single spike), candidates 1–2 show ~3 cycles (three spikes), candidate 3 shows ~5 cycles (five spikes). Minor morphological variation exists: spike width and post-peak decay slope differ slightly, and candidate 2 has one broader, asymmetric spike (1917–1918), while candidate 3 shows a slightly prolonged decay after the fourth spike (2852–2855). These are within acceptable variation; no evidence of sustained anomalies or structural deviation.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 0 for queries with single, clean spikes or short windows (<15 pts); use candidate 1 for moderate-length queries (25–35 pts) needing 3-cycle consensus; candidate 3 is best for longer windows (>45 pts) where multi-spike context matters. Candidate 2 is useful when assessing tolerance for broader spike morphology, but defer to 1 or 3 if query spikes are sharp. If a query shows a spike with prolonged decay or plateau top, compare against candidate 2 and 3—not candidate 0—to avoid false alarms.
